newsitem.title: GERMANY: Focus - Allianz industrial business takes dip.
newsitem.headline: Focus - Allianz industrial business takes dip.

text.p: Allianz AG Holding said on Tuesday its industrial insurance business had dipped since the start of 1995 but it still hoped to expand its leading role in the sector.

Reiner Hagemann, management board chairman of domestic non-life unit Allianz Versicherungs AG, told a news conference the company had suffered a two percent drop in industrial insurance premiums to 2.3 billion marks in 1995 and that the downward trend had continued this year.

"But we can afford a certain period of contraction on a temporary basis," he said, adding that Allianz would pursue tighter cost management, selective risk selection and new products to boost its earnings in the sector.

In Germany, where Allianz has a 25 percent market share in industrial insurance, structural crises in an industry plagued by weak demand and Allianz's own risk-oriented underwriting policy contributed to the decline, Hagemann said.

Hagemann declined to give an earnings breakdown for industrial cover. He said fire insurance was operating generally at a loss in Germany but that Allianz was still satisfied with profits in transport and technical insurance.
Claims remained high in the sector and in fire insurance alone, Allianz had paid out 900 million marks.
Hagemann urged improved corporate risk management and said a study had shown that around 60 percent of German companies were lagging in this respect.
Nonetheless, Allianz, which already deals with more than 70 percent of the 1,000 leading clients worldwide, said it wanted to build up its role in industrial insurance.
"We don't want to shrink our way out of this business, but realise our opportunities through growth as well," Hagemann said.

As well as expanding into German credit insurance via its acquisition of Hermes Kreditversicherungs AG, the group planned to strengthen its industrial business in eastern Europe and planned to achieve premium income there of around 600 million marks in 1996.
